text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Up to 1,400 Canadian Broadcasting Corp staff face axe: English-service budget cuts likely to hit one in four TV enployees, one in three radio.

- Major-General Brian Vernon punished for staff's failings: Vernon, the most senior army officer to be disciplined in the scandals involving the Canadian Airborne Regiment, was the victim off misinformation provided by his subordinates, the report of an internal military investigation discloses.
- Tensions high as Bosnians prepare to vote: Reconciliation low priority in nation torn by ethnic cleansing, civilian murders.
- Obstetricians continue to refuse patients: Orthopedic colleagues suspend protest after Ontario Premier Mike Harris promise to negotiate fees.
- Corruption rules Mexicans' everyday life: From government officials to traffic cops, everyone is for sale. 'The bite' is undermining the legitimacy of the ruling party.
- Ellis-Don buyout collapses: Management bid to buy global construction firm withdrawn because of financial terms.
- Digital plans new, upgraded line of PCs: Recommitment to corporate market 'really good' for Canadian subsidiary.
- EU currency plan puts governments to the test: 15 member nations struggle with fall budgets aimed at putting economies in shape for 1997.
- Iraq, weather wild cards for crude.
- Banks sink Consumers: Banks reject financing offer and put retailer into bankruptcy, leaving unsecured creditors, owed C$150M, high and dry.

- Jobs figures flash optimistic economic signals: Canadian employment surged in August, all but erasing doubt raised by job losses in May and June, and signalling the economy may finally be poised to accelerate into a period of sustained growth.
